approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from previously accepted, scored molecules. It retains at most 64 survivors by score, draws parents from favored score bands, and either recombines connected fragments from two parents or makes a short sequence of ordinary single-parent mutations. A successful crossover receives an additional random finishing mutation with probability 35 percent before it reaches the candidate pool. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Valid, unique proposals fill a fresh surplus pool; a Gaussian process fitted to all earlier accepted scores uses counts of local molecular environments and correlated posterior draws to choose the announced evaluation batch. Accepted offspring update both the model archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Remove only the optional finishing mutation after a successful crossover, retaining its original random gate draw. The immediate recombinant must still pass the ordinary validity, identity and duplicate gates. Earlier siblings removed whole crossover or ordinary single-parent continuation; others changed recombination, parent scheduling or proposal lifetime. None isolates this finishing branch. Finishing can disrupt a completed structure, but the Parent also evaluates useful finished products and breeds from them, so the registered contribution prediction is a score decrease on removal. A complete contrary or negligible result would answer the same narrow question. This finishing-only treatment also supplies the separate control needed to interpret the parallel ring-recombination interaction.

hypothesis: Remove optional post-crossover finishing mutation by setting its existing probability from 0.35 to 0.0 while retaining exactly one original gate draw after every successful ordinary crossover, so its immediate product reaches the unchanged admission pipeline without a finishing call; retain ordinary single-parent continuation and every other active Parent rule.

finding_summary.headline: Finishing contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers the mean despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights:
The complete exposed removal supports a positive contribution from optional finishing in this exact exchange-disabled search composition. Earlier whole-crossover and ordinary-continuation controls did not answer this boundary. Preserving immediate recombinants clearly delivered useful evaluated and breeding products, yet that delivery was insufficient to preserve final search quality. More local wins were measured against weaker generating parents; they cannot substitute for the endpoint comparison. The result remains conditional: the gain in one seed and seven task/seed cells rules out a uniform benefit claim.

The molecules also do not support a simple chemical-preservation explanation. Mean size and ring count increased, but distinct typed core count decreased from 1,851 to 1,749. Tiny fragments and cumulenes became less frequent, while reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persisted alongside useful conventional alternatives. Those are observed changes, not identified causes of the endpoint loss. Observed wall time increased from about 579 to 2,868 seconds, largely alongside higher oracle time on changed molecules, so fewer finishing calls do not establish a compute saving. The separate roles of missing finishing products, altered admission and random streams, and later adaptive feedback remain unresolved. This finding closes the exact finishing contribution question under the tested conditions; it does not establish whole-foundation value or the pending ring-by-finishing interaction.
finding_summary.results:
Finishing was absent at all 35,049 successful crossover opportunities, with 12,346 retained gate draws below the old threshold. Of those exposed immediate products, 9,907 entered candidate pools and 515 reached real evaluation. All 501 nonterminal accepted products entered the next model fit; 297 later bred. Fourteen births were terminal, and 204 other accepted products had later opportunities but were never reused.

All fifteen task/seed comparisons completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.559427, a paired change of -0.036243 against the registered 0.002 loss threshold. Seed changes were -0.059007, +0.020922 and -0.070644; eight task/seed endpoints declined and seven improved. Decoration hopping and docking had the largest mean losses, while zaleplon and median-2 means improved. Seed population dispersion fell from 0.026593 to 0.021675 around the lower mean. Across all accepted offspring, strict parent wins rose from 629 to 689 and incumbent gains from 258 to 264, but absolute offspring and parent scores were lower and the average positive incumbent step fell from 0.022510 to 0.019939.

molecular.overall_character: Assessed Algorithm Node n-5a357a2ac96f against published Parent n-62daf219c70a. All 15 Child and 15 published Parent trajectory files were present and read in full: 9000 records altogether, including 4350 evaluated optimizer proposals on each side. Every task has 900 records, including 870 optimizer proposals, across Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2; tasks_without_trajectories is empty. The immutable brief reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, with all supplied seeds matched and no profile-mismatched seeds. There are no missing paths or absent task/seed comparisons. The final_molecules digest excerpt contains late seed-2 proposals, not every seed incumbent; seed-specific bests and terminal proposals were read from the full files. The output consists of substituted indole/benzimidazole amides and strained arene-fused analogues, linked aza/oxygen polycycles, aryl cyclic amines, medium-ring nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl heterocycles. Across tasks, supplied ring-closure-string incidence is 0.9724 to 0.9931 and aromatic-string incidence is 0.969 to 0.9839. These measure whether a molecule contains the text feature, not its ring count or fraction of aromatic atoms. Halogen-string incidence ranges from 0.2069 to 0.9713. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidence are 0.0 throughout; neutral strings nevertheless contain recognizable protonatable amines. A read-only RDKit 2023.09.6 audit of the trajectory SMILES parsed every evaluated optimizer proposal on both sides. Child heavy-atom counts have median 29 and mean 32.55, versus Parent median 28 and mean 28.71. Child mean perceived ring count is 4.49 versus 3.79, while the median is 4 on both sides. This is substantial cyclic and aromatic chemistry, with saturated nitrogen rings also present. Structural diversity is moderate across seeds and tasks but narrower among leading relatives within a seed; different strings and perceived ring counts do not establish independent useful scaffolds. The same audit finds N-halogen bonds in 1092 Child versus 1042 Parent optimizer records, O-halogen bonds in 545 versus 278, and O-O bonds in 272 versus 273. These are overlapping record-level incidences, not counts of distinct molecules or measurements of reactivity. Carbon-centred cumulated double bonds occur in 6 Child versus 52 Parent records, and proposals with at most 4 heavy atoms number 70 versus 119. Thus several liabilities persist while cumulenes and tiny-fragment exposure are less frequent. No emitted optimizer SMILES on either side contains an explicit tetrahedral or double-bond stereochemical marker; RDKit finds at least one unassigned potential tetrahedral centre in 2214 Child records. Perceived potential stereochemistry does not establish configurational stability. Ordinary aromatic halogens, amides, ethers, lactams and tertiary amines coexist with N-F/N-Cl, O-halogen, peroxide, strained-ring and unusual sulfur environments. Drug-likeness is weak overall and synthesis questionable, although individual conventional functional groups and some leaders are credible starting points for chemistry review. Valid SMILES and high oracle scores do not establish synthesis, stability, conformation or biological activity. The original gap reports for n-c55c3d520a2c and the baseline reproduction n-62daf219c70a were read through context.evidence_index; recurring gaps below preserve that provenance and are newly conditioned on this Child panel. Descriptor definitions, complete source-path hashes, per-seed examples and record-level derived chemistry are in .slots/round-0023-slot-0/molecular/chemistry_audit.json, trajectory_chemistry.jsonl and audit_chemistry.py. method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

finding_summary.headline: Finishing contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers the mean despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights:
The complete exposed removal supports a positive contribution from optional finishing in this exact exchange-disabled search composition. Earlier whole-crossover and ordinary-continuation controls did not answer this boundary. Preserving immediate recombinants clearly delivered useful evaluated and breeding products, yet that delivery was insufficient to preserve final search quality. More local wins were measured against weaker generating parents; they cannot substitute for the endpoint comparison. The result remains conditional: the gain in one seed and seven task/seed cells rules out a uniform benefit claim.

The molecules also do not support a simple chemical-preservation explanation. Mean size and ring count increased, but distinct typed core count decreased from 1,851 to 1,749. Tiny fragments and cumulenes became less frequent, while reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persisted alongside useful conventional alternatives. Those are observed changes, not identified causes of the endpoint loss. Observed wall time increased from about 579 to 2,868 seconds, largely alongside higher oracle time on changed molecules, so fewer finishing calls do not establish a compute saving. The separate roles of missing finishing products, altered admission and random streams, and later adaptive feedback remain unresolved. This finding closes the exact finishing contribution question under the tested conditions; it does not establish whole-foundation value or the pending ring-by-finishing interaction.

finding_summary.headline: Finishing contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers the mean despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights:
The complete exposed removal supports a positive contribution from optional finishing in this exact exchange-disabled search composition. Earlier whole-crossover and ordinary-continuation controls did not answer this boundary. Preserving immediate recombinants clearly delivered useful evaluated and breeding products, yet that delivery was insufficient to preserve final search quality. More local wins were measured against weaker generating parents; they cannot substitute for the endpoint comparison. The result remains conditional: the gain in one seed and seven task/seed cells rules out a uniform benefit claim.

The molecules also do not support a simple chemical-preservation explanation. Mean size and ring count increased, but distinct typed core count decreased from 1,851 to 1,749. Tiny fragments and cumulenes became less frequent, while reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persisted alongside useful conventional alternatives. Those are observed changes, not identified causes of the endpoint loss. Observed wall time increased from about 579 to 2,868 seconds, largely alongside higher oracle time on changed molecules, so fewer finishing calls do not establish a compute saving. The separate roles of missing finishing products, altered admission and random streams, and later adaptive feedback remain unresolved. This finding closes the exact finishing contribution question under the tested conditions; it does not establish whole-foundation value or the pending ring-by-finishing interaction.
finding_summary.results:
Finishing was absent at all 35,049 successful crossover opportunities, with 12,346 retained gate draws below the old threshold. Of those exposed immediate products, 9,907 entered candidate pools and 515 reached real evaluation. All 501 nonterminal accepted products entered the next model fit; 297 later bred. Fourteen births were terminal, and 204 other accepted products had later opportunities but were never reused.

All fifteen task/seed comparisons completed. Mean final Top-1 fell from 0.595670 to 0.559427, a paired change of -0.036243 against the registered 0.002 loss threshold. Seed changes were -0.059007, +0.020922 and -0.070644; eight task/seed endpoints declined and seven improved. Decoration hopping and docking had the largest mean losses, while zaleplon and median-2 means improved. Seed population dispersion fell from 0.026593 to 0.021675 around the lower mean. Across all accepted offspring, strict parent wins rose from 629 to 689 and incumbent gains from 258 to 264, but absolute offspring and parent scores were lower and the average positive incumbent step fell from 0.022510 to 0.019939.

finding_summary.headline: Finishing contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers the mean despite more local wins
finding_summary.insights:
The complete exposed removal supports a positive contribution from optional finishing in this exact exchange-disabled search composition. Earlier whole-crossover and ordinary-continuation controls did not answer this boundary. Preserving immediate recombinants clearly delivered useful evaluated and breeding products, yet that delivery was insufficient to preserve final search quality. More local wins were measured against weaker generating parents; they cannot substitute for the endpoint comparison. The result remains conditional: the gain in one seed and seven task/seed cells rules out a uniform benefit claim.

The molecules also do not support a simple chemical-preservation explanation. Mean size and ring count increased, but distinct typed core count decreased from 1,851 to 1,749. Tiny fragments and cumulenes became less frequent, while reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persisted alongside useful conventional alternatives. Those are observed changes, not identified causes of the endpoint loss. Observed wall time increased from about 579 to 2,868 seconds, largely alongside higher oracle time on changed molecules, so fewer finishing calls do not establish a compute saving. The separate roles of missing finishing products, altered admission and random streams, and later adaptive feedback remain unresolved. This finding closes the exact finishing contribution question under the tested conditions; it does not establish whole-foundation value or the pending ring-by-finishing interaction.
